business_question: How many minutes does a leg lose at hubs beyond driving time, and which centres cause it?
target: handling_min = max(start_scan_to_end_scan - leg actual_time, 0); models trained on log1p

base_rate_or_baseline.metric: training median handling by source centre (MAE, minutes)

winner_reason: LightGBM chosen on MAE (47.5 min). Models within 2% of the best MAE: ['LightGBM']; when several are within 2% the simplest is preferred.

top_drivers.plain_english: source_center: the biggest push toward hub handling time (log minutes) comes from 'IND600056AAB', the biggest push away from it from 'IND302014AAB'.
destination_center: the biggest push toward hub handling time (log minutes) comes from 'IND501359AAE', the biggest push away from it from 'IND401104AAA'.
Higher od_start_hour raises the predicted hub handling time (log minutes).
Higher osrm_distance raises the predicted hub handling time (log minutes).
Higher source_daily_leg_volume raises the predicted hub handling time (log minutes).

caveats: Data is from 2018 and covers about 3 weeks; one test week.
No weather, traffic or hub-staffing data.
No cost fields; the rupee figures use sourced synthetic rates.
source_daily_leg_volume counts legs in this extract only; it is a congestion proxy, not true hub load.
Handling time is derived as scan-to-scan time minus recorded driving time, so recording errors in either appear as handling time.

pi_low / pi_high: LightGBM quantiles calibrated by split-conformal (CQR) on the 21-26 Sep validation slice (Q = 0.176 on the log scale); test coverage of the nominal 80% interval is 79.7% (raw quantiles 68.1%).
